target_customer: Agriculture input companies and growers that buy microbial products to raise yields and cut spoilage
problem: Finding commercially useful microbes in the field is slow, so few microbial products reach the market. Boost used DNA sequencing and informatics to discover them faster.
business_model: Microbial product discovery with joint development and licensing partners such as Yara

founders.name: Rob McBride
founders.background_notes: AgFunder News says he met Bacher at Sapphire Energy, an algae biofuel company.

founders.name: Jamie Bacher
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page; described as CEO in 2018 coverage.

founders.name: Adam Arkin
founders.background_notes: AgFunder News says he contributed the DNA sequencing discovery process. Further background not found in an opened source.

competitors.name: Pivot Bio
competitors.what: Engineered nitrogen fixing microbes to replace fertilizer
competitors.funding_then: $70M round led by Bill Gates's fund, Oct 2018

competitors.name: Indigo Ag
competitors.what: Microbial seed treatments and ag biologicals

technical_complexity.rationale: Discovering functional microbes by sequencing, enrichment and informatics, then turning them into field-tested products, needs deep biology and years of trials.

defensibility.rationale: A discovery platform and strain library are hard to copy, but well funded rivals like Pivot Bio and Indigo were already in the space.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copying found. Yara became a development partner and investor in 2020.

market_need_then: Growers and fertilizer companies were funding microbial alternatives in 2018; Yara committed $3M in 2020 to co-develop a nutrient uptake product.

brand_strength.rationale: Coverage was trade press only (AgFunder, Global AgInvesting, TechCrunch). The name is clear but no brand assets or community were found.

outcome_analysis: Boost Biomes raised about $2.05M seed in 2018, a $5M Series A led by Yara in June 2020 and a $2M extension in December 2020, and signed a joint development deal with Yara. YC now lists it as inactive but no shutdown, acquisition or post-mortem was found, so the cause and date of the stall are not public and no failure factors are assigned. The last company specific material found dates from around 2021.
notes: Seed amount conflicts: AgFunder says $2.05M, another outlet says $2.5M; $2.05M used. Total funding conflicts across databases (ZoomInfo $9.1M). One search snippet said Series A exceeded $7.5M including the extension. The company was founded in 2016, before the Summer 2019 batch. Seed 2020-02 Kureha amount not disclosed. Funding coverage is partial because later rounds, if any, were not found. Confidence is set to medium-level evidence on competition (two dated competitors from one article).
